scientific_name: Iterative mean-centered sigma clipping with complete retained mask
common_name: Iterative mean-centered sigma clipping with complete retained mask
scientific_use: Reject outliers and estimate background statistics for astronomical image patches or time-series windows.
scientific_purpose: Reject outliers and estimate background statistics for astronomical image patches or time-series windows.

source_references.title: Astropy sigma_clip, mean center and population standard deviation
Berkeley SoftFloat: software IEEE arithmetic methodology (no code copied)

canonical_equations: For retained set: mu=ordered_sum(x)/n; v=ordered_sum((x-mu)^2)/n; bounds=mu-sigma_lower*sqrt(v),mu+sigma_upper*sqrt(v); reject strictly outside simultaneously; repeat until stable or maxiters; recompute final statistics; all operations RN32.
input_contract: encoding=binary32-hex; samples[B,N],valid[B,N] uint0/1; B1..128,N1..512; sigma_lower/upper finite>=0; maxiters1..16; B*N*maxiters<=1048576; all RN32 intermediates finite.
output_contract: B x [status,u32 retained_count,binary32 mean,binary32 population_variance,N uint retained_flags]; status0 stable,1 empty,2 last allowed iteration removed values; empty mean/variance/mask are positive zero.
result_contract: B x [status,u32 retained_count,binary32 mean,binary32 population_variance,N uint retained_flags]; status0 stable,1 empty,2 last allowed iteration removed values; empty mean/variance/mask are positive zero.
precision_requirements: Finite IEEE binary32 values, explicitly supplied as eight hex digits (encoding=binary32-hex). Every +,-,*,/,sqrt rounds to nearest ties-to-even; gradual underflow; canonical positive zero after arithmetic. No FMA or reassociation. Nonfinite inputs, intermediate overflow, division by zero and invalid roots reject the job on CPU before dispatch. Bit identity is to this specified rounded algorithm, not exact real arithmetic or other library reduction orders.
validation_method: Full byte comparison against independent exact-rational RN32 CPU oracle; analytic, adversarial and held-out vectors; arithmetic tested separately.
